decisions.quote:
Most remarkably, our exact replication attempts that should have 
had sufficient power according to sample size calculations based on the original papers, did not provide robust 
evidence for amnesia either.  

We can conclude that our findings are in stark contrast with the existing literature on post-reactivation amnesia 
in rats, in which systemic administration of MDZ (Table 1), PROP (Table 2), or CYCLO (Haubrich et al., 2015)  has 
been shown to induce amnesia for contextual fear memories or other types of memories (Briggs & Olson, 2013; 
Dębiec & Ledoux, 2004; Flint & Marino, 2007; Milton, Lee, & Everitt, 2008; Przybyslawski et al., 1999; Robinson 
& Franklin, 2010; Taubenfeld et al., 2009).
decisions.reason: This replication study directly and conceptually re-tests Alfei et al. (2015; listed in Table 1) across five exact replication attempts of Experiment 5 (JA09-JA12, NS09), conceptual variations (NS10, NS12-NS14, NS18, NS21, JA01, JA02), and an extinction consolidation test (NS14). Although two original-lab exact replications (JA11, JA12) reached significance on a one-sided t-test (while failing to reach significance on the original two-sided t-test, p = 0.096 and p = 0.074, and providing only anecdotal Bayesian support, BF10 = 2.07 and 2.50) and all other exact and conceptual replications found no effect, under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1 and the multi-study aggregation rule the authors' explicit overall verdict governs: they conclude that the exact replication attempts 'did not provide robust evidence for amnesia either', state that their findings are 'in stark contrast' with the Table 1 MDZ literature, and characterize their attempts as 'failures to replicate successful studies despite our efforts to follow their methodology as closely as possible'.

Third,  in  experiment  NS11,  an  exact  replication  of  Stern  et  al.  (2012),  freezing  scores  observed  during  the 
reactivation session were consistent with those obtained in the original paper, suggesting successful and similar 
fear acquisition. However, visual inspection of the graphs (Fig. 2 and Appendix C, Fig. C.2F) shows that SAL rats 
showed lower freezing at test compared to MDZ rats, a pattern opposite to the findings reported in the original 
paper.
decisions.reason: Stern et al. (2012) is listed in Table 1 (p. 3, Lab III, Exp. 1, Fig. 1A; 3-min reactivation, 1.5 mg/kg systemic post-reactivation MDZ, N = 15, d = 1.49) and was directly retested in a dedicated preregistered exact replication (Experiment NS11; Methods 2.9.3, pp. 7-8; Results 3.2, p. 11; Fig. 2, p. 12), which found no amnestic effect of post-reactivation MDZ compared to saline (one-tailed t-test: t(10) = .57, p = .709, d = .33, BF10 = .34). It is distinct from shipped row 2487 (Alfei et al., 2015, which was replicated in NS9).
